BiblicalUsage: Maggephah is the plague, the pestilence, and it falls where sin has broken out and is stayed where atonement is made. Numbers 16:48 has Aaron standing between the dead and the living, and the plague was stayed, and Numbers 25:9 counts twenty and four thousand dead in the plague. 2 Samuel 24:25 has David building an altar and the plague stayed from Israel, and Psalms 106:30 remembers Phinehas standing up and executing judgment, and so the plague was stayed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the plague in these verses is never random: it follows sin, and it stops at intercession. My position is that Aaron in Numbers 16:48 and Phinehas in Psalms 106:30 show me what to do when judgment is spreading, which is to stand in the gap, not to run from it.
